title: Does Thunderbird have a way to manually expunge a mailbox?
creator: jms12
content:
Most other email clients I've used have had a way to manually "expunge" a mailbox, i.e. delete the messages which are marked for deletion. This includes Thunderbird on a machine at home (I'm traveling right now).

On this laptop I'm using Thunderbird 102.12.0 on macOS 26.6.2. All of my mailboxes use IMAP. Thunderbird is using Maildir for local storage on this laptop, and I believe the same is true on the machine at home (also macOS 26.6.x, not sure of the exact Thunderbird version), but I won't be able to verify this until I get home tomorrow evening.

On both machines, when I delete a message, the message list shows that message with a line through it, corresponding to the IMAP "marked for deletion" flag. The same is true on the other email clients I've used over the years.

On the machine at home , when I right-click on an account's "Inbox" folder, there is a "Compress folder" option which expunges the deleted messages from the mailbox. This option is not present in Thunderbird on this laptop.

So my questions are ...

  • Is the menu item I'm talking about, only present when the account uses MBOX for local storage, and maybe I missed a step when I created the account on the machine at home? (If so, I know how to fix that when I get home.)
  • Every email client I remember using, all the way back to the original `pine` in the mid-1990's, has had an "expunge" command of some kind. Does Thunderbird really not have a way to manually expunge a mailbox? If so, this seems like a fundamental oversight on the part of the Mozilla developers.
  • Or is there a way to do it, and my old eyes just aren't seeing it on the menus? (which is entirely possible)

Thanks.

(Side question, totally unrelated) ... why does the text entry control I'm typing this message into, have its own markup language instead of using standard Markdown? (And yes I am, at least in part, being old and gumbly here ... you kids get off my lawn!)

title: Thunderbird impazzito
creator: filippomazzoccu
content: Buongiorno, ho un problema molto grave con Thunderbird e un account Yahoo configurato in imap(sempre funzionato). Quando Thunderbird inizia a scaricare la posta di Yahoo, scarica correttamente le mie email, circa 20.000 messaggi. Il problema è che, al termine del download,,una volta eliminati,li riscarica assieme a centinaia di messaggi anomali. Questi messaggi hanno tutti le seguenti caratteristiche: • nessun oggetto • nessun mittente • 0 KB • data 01/01/1970 • ora 01:00 • risultano associati al mio account Yahoo Se li cancello, ricompaiono nuovamente. Inoltre Thunderbird continua a riscaricare continuamente le stesse email già scaricate, anche se le elimino dalla posta locale. La cosa più importante è che ho già effettuato una reinstallazione completamente pulita di Thunderbird. Ho già provato: 1. eliminazione dell'account Yahoo da Thunderbird; 2. eliminazione del profilo Thunderbird; 3. eliminazione delle cartelle e dei file di Thunderbird; 4. eliminazione dei file .msf, compreso Inbox.msf; 5. disinstallazione completa di Thunderbird; 6. reinstallazione di Thunderbird; 7. creazione di un nuovo profilo; 8. configurazione nuovamente dell'account Yahoo in imap. Nonostante tutto questo, il problema si ripresenta identico. Quindi non credo che si tratti semplicemente di un indice .msf corrotto o di un vecchio profilo Thunderbird. Vorrei capire se il problema può essere causato dal protocollo imap di Yahoo, in particolare dalla gestione degli identificativi UIDL o dal file/stato che Thunderbird utilizza per ricordare quali messaggi sono già stati scaricati. La situazione attuale è questa: Yahoo Webmail → le email sono normali e leggibili. Thunderbird imap → scarica le email, ma continua a riscaricare messaggi già scaricati e genera migliaia di messaggi vuoti da 0 KB con data 01/01/1970. Vorrei quindi sapere: • È possibile che Yahoo stia inviando tramite imap dei dati corrotti o non validi? • È possibile che Thunderbird non riesca a interpretare correttamente l'UIDL di alcuni messaggi? • Esiste un modo per verificare cosa sta realmente ricevendo Thunderbird dal server imap? • C'è qualche file diverso dagli .msf che memorizza lo stato dei messaggi imap già scaricati? • È un problema già conosciuto con Yahoo? • Quali log o informazioni tecniche posso fornire per permettere di individuare il problema? Non vorrei continuare a reinstallare Thunderbird o cancellare il profilo, perché ho già eseguito questa procedura più volte e il problema ritorna anche con un profilo completamente nuovo. Grazie a chiunque possa aiutarmi a capire se il problema è in Thunderbird

title: Sent message remains in Drafts and is not saved in Sent folder
creator: fririru
content:
I have a recurring problem with Thunderbird 153.2.0esr (64-bit).

After clicking the Send button, the message is successfully sent to the recipients. I can see that the sending process takes place, and I have confirmed that the message was actually delivered because I was one of the recipients myself and several BCC recipients have replied to it.

However, after sending, the message sometimes does not appear in the Sent folder. Instead, it remains in the Drafts folder.

This is particularly problematic because it gives the impression that the message may not have been sent, although it actually has been delivered. There is therefore a risk of sending the same message again by mistake.

The problem occurs only occasionally. The most recent occurrence involved an email sent to approximately 180 recipients via BCC with an attachment of about 1.8 MB.

title: U4GM POE 2 Forbidden Rites Launch Guide
creator: pontiggiafrancesca127
content:
Path of Exile 2 is entering a stage where smart preparation matters as much as fast reactions. Whether you are building a new character or refining an established one, reliable POE 2 Items can make the journey through difficult areas smoother and more rewarding.

The sequel places greater emphasis on timing, positioning, and meaningful equipment choices. A strong character is not simply the one with the highest damage number; it is the one that can survive pressure while keeping its abilities consistent.

Why Equipment Planning Matters Early upgrades should focus on practical improvements rather than perfect statistics. Life, resistances, weapon quality, and useful support effects usually provide more value than a small increase to one offensive attribute. This approach also leaves room for later adjustments as the skill setup becomes clearer.

Players should review their equipment after every major story milestone. New areas often introduce stronger enemies with different damage types, so an item that felt excellent several hours ago may no longer cover the character's most urgent weakness.

Equipment Area Primary Concern Useful Secondary Goal Weapon Consistent damage Attribute or skill support Body Armour Life and defenses Resistance balance Accessories Missing attributes Resource recovery Building a Reliable Combat Routine Combat becomes more manageable when every skill has a clear purpose. A main attack should be supported by one movement option, one defensive response, and at least one ability that controls groups or interrupts dangerous enemies.

Instead of using every skill whenever it becomes available, watch enemy patterns first. Many encounters reward patience. Dodging a heavy strike, creating distance, and then returning with a focused attack often produces better results than standing still and repeating one action.

Managing Currency and Inventory Space Inventory discipline is an underrated part of progression. Keep items that offer a meaningful improvement, but avoid carrying every object that might become useful someday. A compact inventory makes town visits faster and reduces the time spent comparing minor upgrades.

Currency should be spent with a clear goal. Improving a promising weapon or repairing a defensive gap is usually more valuable than making constant low-impact changes. Before committing resources, compare the current item with the best available alternative and consider how long the upgrade is likely to remain relevant.

Preparing for Difficult Encounters Before entering a demanding area, check resistances, flask charges, available movement skills, and the distance to the nearest safe checkpoint. Preparation is especially important when an encounter includes several enemy types, since a character designed for close combat may struggle against persistent ranged pressure.

A simple checklist can prevent unnecessary setbacks.

Confirm that core resistances are not falling behind. Carry recovery options suited to the area. Test the main skill against both single targets and groups. Leave room for an emergency defensive change. Path of Exile 2 rewards players who treat progression as a series of small decisions rather than a race toward one perfect build. With careful upgrades, controlled spending, and a flexible combat plan, each area becomes easier to read and more enjoyable to master. For players looking to prepare their next step, well-chosen Path of Exile 2 Items can support that plan while keeping the focus on exploration and satisfying combat.

title: Email filter problem after update
creator: robinson77
content: I'm new to the community and don't really know how things work, so maybe this is the wrong place for this. I had a seemingly catastrophic problem after updating yesterday. All of the emails sitting in my inbox disappeared, and were gone from the yahoo server as well. Long story short, I figured out what happened. In my filter rules I sometimes had a blank entry at the end of the list. Previously that had been ignored, but after the update it is now treated as a match. So the first filter that had a blank in it caused everything in my inbox to be moved to a certain folder in my Local Folders. Obviously, it would be legitimate to not allow blank entries in the filters, but once you've allowed it, you really shouldn't make a change. In the end the solution was simple, but it wasted a fair portion of my day figuring it out.
